question: Should OpenClaw expose optional one-shot reset correlation on the shared agent-harness reset and plugin session-end contracts for owner plugins such as Codex?
rationale: The implementation needs core to carry information from the successful harness reset to the later plugin lifecycle hook. Whether that shared seam is an acceptable permanent contract is a product and ownership decision, not a mechanical correctness question.

options.title: Accept the shared reset correlation
options.body: Accept the optional transient token as a generic lifecycle contract and merge this narrowly scoped Codex fix after refreshing the branch.

options.title: Keep correlation plugin-owned
options.body: Require a different owner-specific lifecycle seam, avoiding new shared hook and harness fields at the cost of redesigning the reset notification path.

recommendation.title: Accept the shared reset correlation
recommendation.body: Accept the optional transient token as a generic lifecycle contract and merge this narrowly scoped Codex fix after refreshing the branch.

likelyOwner.reason: The durable reset design that preserves physical session IDs was introduced by this owner, making them the clearest available decision route for the cross-boundary lifecycle contract.
